case_name: Safi Mohd. v State of Rajasthan
respondent:
State of Rajasthan
Supreme Court of India

17 April 2013
Cr.A. No. 1954 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : V. Gopala Gowda, J.
1. This appeal is filed by the appellant questioning the correctness of the judgment dated 29th May, 2009 passed by the High Court of Rajasthan at Jaipur in S.B. Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2004 in confirming the judgment dated 9th March, 2004 of the sessions judge, Jaipur City, Jaipur in Sessions Case No. 196 of 1992 wherein this appellant along with the
facts: On 6th March, 1990, Bhoormal Jain, Superintendent of Police CID Zone, Jodhpur lodged an FIR for the offences punishable under Sections 3, 3/9 of the Act read with Section 120-B IPC with the Special Police Station Rajasthan, Jaipur numbered as FIR No.1/1990 against the accused Mohd.
On interrogation, he stated that the appellant Safi Mohd. used to supply secret information to the Pakistani Intelligence and had handed over Rs.6500/- to him for working for Pak Intelligence Agency.
Later on, on further disclosure by the accused No.1, accused No.3 - Chotu Khan and accused No.4 - Chand Khan were arrested.
On 12.04.1990, the other accused Mohd. Safi, Accused No.5, was also arrested.
issues: The correctness of the judgment dated 29th May, 2009 passed by the High Court of Rajasthan at Jaipur in S.B. Criminal Appeal No. 314 of 2004
Whether the conviction based on the recovery of Ex.D-3 from the house of the appellant is doubtful
petitioner_arguments: The conviction of the appellant based on the recovery of Ex.D-3 from the house of the appellant is doubtful.
The conviction based on the experts' opinion of Col S.K. Sareen (PW-27) and Wing Commander Alok Kumar (PW-32) on documents Ex.P-33 and P-34 respectively is not in favour of the prosecution.
The recovery of the document Ex.D-3 from the quarters of appellant is attested by two witnesses Bhoop Singh and Umed Singh, but Umed Singh has not been examined in the case.
The prosecution has relied upon the said document solely on the statement of evidence of the investigating officer Yad Ram Tiwari PW-24 and Suresh Kumar PW-22.
respondent_arguments: The documents recovered from the accused were sent to the Air Force Officers for their opinion, who informed that the said documents were useful to enemy country and affect the security of India.
The learned Sessions Judge after trial convicted the appellant u/s 3 (1) (c) of the Act by order dated 09.03.2004.
court_reasoning: The non-examination of Umed Singh, the attesting witness to the memo for recovery of the documents from the house of the appellant, is a serious irregularity that should have been taken into account by the courts below.
The evidence of PW-2 who is the owner of the Rathi Guest House, has admitted in his statement that 'Map Ex.D-3 was recovered from the said accused along with other papers.'
The defence is not required to establish its case but is only required to establish preponderance of probabilities of the case for consideration of the Court.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the conviction of the appellant is set aside.
